title: PAC-Causal Learnability: From Identification to Finite-Sample Guarantees
abstract: arXiv:2507.18903v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Causal identification asks whether a causal target can be recovered from the observational distribution in an idealized infinite-data setting. In practice, only finite samples are available, and identifiability alone does not determine how much data are needed for reliable estimation. We introduce Probably Approximately Correct Causal (PACC) learnability, which formalizes uniform accuracy-confidence guarantees over a causal model class. From a PAC-learning perspective, we ask how many samples are sufficient to estimate a causal target to accuracy $\epsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. We show that PACC sample complexity is shaped by three recurring factors: causal identification strength, target complexity, and nuisance complexity, and derive a general sufficient bound linking them to finite-sample causal learning. translated_title: PAC因果可学习性：从识别到有限样本保证
translated_abstract: 因果识别探讨的是在理想化的无限数据设定下，能否从观测分布中恢复出因果目标。在实践中，只有有限样本可用，而可识别性本身并不能确定可靠估计需要多少数据。我们引入了“可能近似正确因果”（PACC）可学习性，它在因果模型类上形式化了统一的精度-置信度保证。从PAC学习的视角出发，我们探究需要多少样本才能以至少1-δ的概率将因果目标估计到精度ε。我们证明PACC样本复杂度由三个反复出现的因素决定：因果识别强度、目标复杂度和干扰复杂度，并推导出一个将三者与有限样本因果学习联系起来的通用充分界。我们通过自身对照病例系列、工具变量和倾向性（评分）方法来阐述该框架。
tldr: 该论文提出了PACC因果可学习性框架，首次从PAC学习角度为因果估计提供了有限样本的统一精度-置信度保证，并揭示其样本复杂度由因果识别强度、目标复杂度和干扰复杂度三个关键因素决定。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PACC causal learnability, a PAC-learning framework providing uniform finite-sample accuracy-confidence guarantees for causal estimation, and shows its sample complexity is governed by causal identification strength, target complexity, and nuisance complexity.
